The Spanish laúd is a plucked chordophone from Spain, also played in countries of the diaspora such as Cuba and the Philippines, Hornbostel–Sachs number 321.322. It belongs to the cittern family; the Spanish and Cuban versions have six pairs of strings in unison, twelve strings in all; the Philippine version has fourteen strings, some single and some triple. It is traditionally used by folk string groups such as the Spanish or Philippine rondalla, playing with the guitar and the bandurria. Its tuning is mostly in fourths, and its range lies an octave below the bandurria.

西班牙琵琶為撥奏弦鳴樂器，源自西班牙，也在古巴、菲律賓等離散地區使用。傳統上出現: The Spanish lute (laúd) is a plucked chordophone from Spain, also used in diaspora communities in Cuba and the Philippines. It traditionally appears in folk string groups such as the Spanish or Philippine rondalla, together with the guitar and the bandurria. The Cuban laúd looks and functions much the same, with a shorter scale and a higher tuning; the Philippine version has fourteen strings and is tuned a step lower than the Spanish.
西班牙琵琶的共鳴箱採用優質木材製成，通常為雲杉或松木製作面板，提供溫暖的音響特性: The soundbox of the Spanish laúd is made of good timber, usually a top of spruce or pine, which gives a warm tone. The back and sides are mostly hardwoods such as maple, plane or ebony to strengthen the resonance. The neck is of a hard wood such as rosewood or ebony. The strings are silk or gut, with some of the treble strings bare copper or copper-wound. The tuning keys and pegs are of ivory or hardwood, and the careful workmanship ensures the instrument's durability and its tone.
西班牙琵琶音色溫潤而富有光澤，兼具明亮與深邃的特質。其音域寬廣，從低音的溫暖厚重: The Spanish laúd has a warm, lustrous tone that is both bright and deep. Its range is wide, from a warm, heavy bass to a clear, shining treble, with many layers. The wooden soundbox resonates and produces a full sound, so that the energy of the vibrating strings is amplified and carried. Compared with the Italian instruments the Spanish laúd is gentler and quieter; compared with the guitar its tone carries further and has the bleakness of age. Plucked, it can give out a cold metallic gleam and also the softness of a string instrument. These qualities make it especially suited to Spanish folk music and classical pieces, and let it convey artistry and dramatic tension.
